```{r}
# Function to install and load packages 
package_install = function(package_list) {
  for (pkg in package_list) {
    if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
      tryCatch({
        install.packages(pkg)
      }, error = function(e) {
        message(paste0("Could not install ", pkg, ": ", e))
      })
    }
    # Load the library
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
  }
}
```

```{r}
# Function to process and rename exposure data
process_exposure_data = function(period_key, suffix) {
  # Find keys that start with the given period_key
  key_match = grep(paste0("^", period_key), names(combined_exposure_data), value = TRUE)
  
  # Check if a matching key was found
  if (length(key_match) == 0) {
    stop("No matching key for ", period_key, " found in combined_exposure_data")
  }
  
  # Use the first matching key (assuming there is only one that fits)
  combined_exposure_data[[ key_match[1] ]]$data %>%
    select(person_id, 
           C1M_School_closing,
           C2M_Workplace_closing,
           C3M_Cancel_public_events,
           C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings,
           C5M_Close_public_transport,
           C6M_Stay_at_home_requirements,
           C7M_Restrictions_on_internal_movement) %>%
    rename_with(~ paste0(., suffix), -person_id)
}

# Simple function to check policy ranges 
check_policy_ranges = function(data) {
  # Identify policy columns
  policy_cols = grep("C[1-7]M", names(data), value = TRUE)
  
  # Print header
  cat("\n=== COVID Policy Range Check ===\n")
  
  # Check each policy column
  all_integer = TRUE
  
  for (col in policy_cols) {
    values = data[[col]]
    min_val = min(values, na.rm = TRUE)
    max_val = max(values, na.rm = TRUE)
    is_integer = all(values == round(values), na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Get value counts
    value_counts = table(values)
    count_text = paste(paste0(names(value_counts), ":", value_counts), collapse=", ")
    
    # If any non-integer values are found, update the flag
    if (!is_integer) {
      all_integer = FALSE
    }
    
    # Print the results
    cat(sprintf("%-50s: Range [%g-%g], Integer-only: %s\n", 
                col, min_val, max_val, 
                ifelse(is_integer, "Yes", "No")))
  }
  
  # Overall result
  cat("\nAll policies have integer-only values: ", 
      ifelse(all_integer, "YES", "NO"), "\n\n")
}
```

# Functions

```{r}
#' Create a single stratified train/test split
#' 
#' This function creates a train/test split using either manual stratified sampling
#' or tidymodels approach. The manual method stratifies by region_final and gad_category,
#' randomly ordering observations within each stratum and allocating 50% to training.
#' 
#' @param data The full dataset to split
#' @param seed_value Seed for reproducible randomization
#' @param method Either "manual" for custom stratified sampling or "tidymodels" for rsample approach
#' @return List containing train_data, test_data, and seed value
create_stratified_split = function(data, seed_value, method = "manual") {
  set.seed(seed_value)
  
  if(method == "manual") {
    # Manual stratified sampling: stratify by region and GAD category
    stratified_data = data %>%
      group_by(region_final, gad_category) %>%
      mutate(random_order = runif(n())) %>%  # Random ordering within strata
      arrange(random_order) %>%
      mutate(
        stratum_size = n(),
        train_size = floor(stratum_size * 0.50),  # 50% to training, rounded down
        train_flag = row_number() <= train_size
      ) %>%
      ungroup()
    
    train_data = stratified_data %>% filter(train_flag == TRUE)
    test_data = stratified_data %>% filter(train_flag == FALSE)
    
  } else if(method == "tidymodels") {
    # Using tidymodels initial_split with stratification
    data_split = initial_split(data, prop = 0.50, strata = "strata_var", pool = 0.05)
    train_data = training(data_split)
    test_data = testing(data_split)
  }
  
  return(list(train = train_data, test = test_data, seed = seed_value))
}

#' Calculate balance score using logistic regression AUC
#' 
#' This function measures how well covariates can predict whether an observation
#' is in the training or test set. Lower AUC (closer to 0.5) indicates better
#' balance, as covariates cannot distinguish between train/test groups.
#' This is the key metric for rerandomization selection.
#' 
#' @param train_data Training dataset
#' @param test_data Test dataset  
#' @param covariates Vector of covariate names to include in balance model
#' @return List with AUC value and diagnostic information
calculate_balance_auc = function(train_data, test_data, covariates) {
  # Combine datasets with group indicator (0=train, 1=test)
  combined_data = bind_rows(
    train_data %>% select(all_of(covariates)) %>% mutate(group = 0),
    test_data %>% select(all_of(covariates)) %>% mutate(group = 1)
  )
  
  # Remove rows with any missing values in covariates
  complete_data = combined_data %>% 
    select(all_of(c(covariates, "group"))) %>%
    na.omit()
  
  if(nrow(complete_data) < 50) {
    warning("Insufficient complete observations for AUC calculation")
    return(list(auc = NA, n_complete = nrow(complete_data)))
  }
  
  # Convert categorical variables to factors for modeling
  for(covar in covariates) {
    if(covar %in% names(complete_data)) {
      if(is.character(complete_data[[covar]]) || is.factor(complete_data[[covar]])) {
        complete_data[[covar]] = factor(complete_data[[covar]])
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Build formula - include all available covariates
  # No restriction on categorical levels since our max is 9 levels
  formula_parts = character(0)
  for(covar in covariates) {
    if(covar %in% names(complete_data)) {
      formula_parts = c(formula_parts, covar)
    }
  }
  
  if(length(formula_parts) == 0) {
    warning("No suitable covariates for balance regression")
    return(list(auc = NA, n_complete = nrow(complete_data)))
  }
  
  # Create logistic regression formula: group ~ all_covariates
  formula_str = paste("group ~", paste(formula_parts, collapse = " + "))
  
  # Fit logistic regression predicting train/test assignment from covariates
  tryCatch({
    balance_model = glm(as.formula(formula_str), 
                        data = complete_data, 
                        family = binomial())
    
    # Get predicted probabilities of being in test set
    predictions = predict(balance_model, type = "response")
    
    # Calculate AUC: How well can covariates predict train/test assignment?
    # AUC near 0.5 = poor prediction = good balance
    # AUC near 1.0 = excellent prediction = poor balance
    auc_result = pROC::auc(complete_data$group, predictions, quiet = TRUE)
    
    return(list(
      auc = as.numeric(auc_result), 
      n_complete = nrow(complete_data),
      n_predictors = length(formula_parts),
      model_converged = balance_model$converged
    ))
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning(paste("Error in balance regression:", e$message))
    return(list(auc = NA, n_complete = nrow(complete_data)))
  })
}

#' Perform rerandomization to find optimal train/test split
#' 
#' This function generates multiple candidate train/test splits and selects
#' the one with the best covariate balance (lowest AUC). This addresses
#' the concern that random chance imbalance could drive differences in
#' policy effect estimates between training and test sets.
#' 
#' @param data Full dataset to split
#' @param n_randomizations Number of candidate splits to generate (5-10 recommended)
#' @param method Splitting method ("manual" or "tidymodels")
#' @return List containing best split, all results, and diagnostics
perform_rerandomization = function(data, n_randomizations = 10, method = "manual") {
  cat("Performing rerandomization with", n_randomizations, "random splits...\n")
  
  # Generate unique seeds for reproducible randomization
  set.seed(42) # Set seed for reproducible results across different exposure windows
  seeds = sample(1:100000, n_randomizations)
  
  # Initialize storage for results
  randomization_results = tibble()
  splits_list = list()
  
  # Progress bar for user feedback
  pb = txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = n_randomizations, style = 3)
  
  # Generate and evaluate each candidate split
  for(i in 1:n_randomizations) {
    setTxtProgressBar(pb, i)
    
    # Create stratified split with unique seed
    split_result = create_stratified_split(data, seeds[i], method)
    splits_list[[i]] = split_result
    
    # Calculate balance AUC for this split
    balance_result = calculate_balance_auc(
      split_result$train, 
      split_result$test, 
      existing_covariates
    )
    
    # Store results for comparison
    randomization_results = bind_rows(randomization_results, tibble(
      randomization = i,
      seed = seeds[i],
      auc = balance_result$auc,
      n_complete = balance_result$n_complete,
      n_predictors = balance_result$n_predictors %||% NA,
      model_converged = balance_result$model_converged %||% NA,
      train_n = nrow(split_result$train),
      test_n = nrow(split_result$test)
    ))
  }
  
  close(pb)
  
  # Find best randomization: lowest AUC indicates best balance
  best_randomization = randomization_results %>%
    filter(!is.na(auc)) %>%
    slice_min(auc, n = 1) %>%
    slice(1)  # In case of ties, take the first
  
  if(nrow(best_randomization) == 0) {
    stop("No valid randomizations found. Check data and covariates.")
  }
  
  cat("\n=== results of rerandomization ===\n")
  cat("Number of valid randomizations:", sum(!is.na(randomization_results$auc)), "\n")
  cat("AUC range:", round(range(randomization_results$auc, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
  cat("Best randomization:", best_randomization$randomization, "\n")
  cat("Best AUC (lower is better):", round(best_randomization$auc, 4), "\n")
  cat("Best seed:", best_randomization$seed, "\n\n")
  
  # Return best split and all results for analysis
  best_split = splits_list[[best_randomization$randomization]]
  
  return(list(
    best_split = best_split,
    all_results = randomization_results,
    best_randomization = best_randomization,
    all_splits = splits_list
  ))
}

```




# Loop for exposure windows

```{r}
# Initialize windows
period_keys <- c("20200315_20200627", "20200322_20200523", "20200412_20200523")
suffixes <-c("_March_15_June_27", "_March_22_May_23", "_April_12_May_23")
stringency_keys <- c("march_15_june_30", "march_22_may_23", "april_12_may_23")

# # For check
# period_keys <- c("20200315_20200627")
# suffixes <-c("_March_15_June_27")
# stringency_keys <- c("march_15_june_30")
# i = 1

results_est_list <- list()
results_hicc_list <- list()


for (i in seq_along(period_keys)) {
  
  # Process exposure window 
  exposure_data <- process_exposure_data(
    period_keys[i],
    suffixes[i]
  )
  
  # Checking policy ranges 
  check_policy_ranges(exposure_data)
  
  # Merge exposure data into main dataframe
  cope_auo_windows = cope_auo %>%
  left_join(exposure_data, by = "person_id") 

  message("Processed and merged for: ", period_keys[i])

  # Verify new columns
  message("New columns added:")
  print(colnames(cope_auo_windows))
  
  # Checking structure of cope_auo data with windows added
  str(cope_auo_windows)
  
  # Ensure each row is a unique individual
  cope_auo_unique = cope_auo_windows %>%
    distinct(person_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
  
  # Build the exposure column names dynamically from the suffixes
  exposure_columns <- c()
  exposure_columns <- c(exposure_columns,
    paste0("C1M_School_closing", suffixes[i]),
    paste0("C2M_Workplace_closing", suffixes[i]),
    paste0("C3M_Cancel_public_events", suffixes[i]),
    paste0("C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings", suffixes[i]),
    paste0("C5M_Close_public_transport", suffixes[i]),
    paste0("C6M_Stay_at_home_requirements", suffixes[i]),
    paste0("C7M_Restrictions_on_internal_movement", suffixes[i])
  )

  
  # Creating a merged dataset using columns of interest from cope_auo_unique and conditions_df
  # Note that conditions_df contains the propensity score values and some covariates of interest
  cope_auo_ps = cope_auo_unique %>%
    select(
      person_id,
      RegionName,
      StringencyIndex_Average_202005,
      gad_score_avg_july,
      date_of_birth,
      age_2020,
      C1M_School_closing,
      C2M_Workplace_closing,
      C3M_Cancel_public_events,
      C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings,
      C5M_Close_public_transport,
      C6M_Stay_at_home_requirements,
      C7M_Restrictions_on_internal_movement,
      # specifically generated exposure columns
      all_of(exposure_columns),
      gad_score_july,
      gad_score_avg_may,
      gad_score_may,
      gad_score_avg_june,
      gad_score_june
    ) %>%
    inner_join(
      conditions_df %>% 
        select(
          person_id,
          anxiety_disorder_before_covid_lifetime,
          generalized_anxiety_disorder_before_covid_lifetime,
          anxiety_disorder_1yr_before_covid,
          generalized_anxiety_disorder_1yr_before_covid,
          response_prob,
          observation_wt,
          observation_wt_trim,
          sex,
          education,
          employment,
          insurance,
          home,
          income,
          maritalstatus,
          race,
          birthplace
        ),
      by = "person_id"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      log_observation_wt = log(observation_wt)
    )
  
  # Check uniqueness in cope_auo_unique (should be TRUE because of distinct())
  n_unique_cope = n_distinct(cope_auo_unique$person_id)
  n_total_cope = nrow(cope_auo_unique)
  all_unique_cope = n_unique_cope == n_total_cope
  
  cat("cope_auo_unique:\n",
      "- Total rows:", n_total_cope, "\n",
      "- Unique person_ids:", n_unique_cope, "\n",
      "- All person_ids unique?:", ifelse(all_unique_cope, "Yes", "No"), "\n\n")
  
  # Check uniqueness in conditions_df
  n_unique_conditions = n_distinct(conditions_df$person_id)
  n_total_conditions = nrow(conditions_df)
  all_unique_conditions = n_unique_conditions == n_total_conditions
  
  cat("conditions_df:\n",
      "- Total rows:", n_total_conditions, "\n",
      "- Unique person_ids:", n_unique_conditions, "\n",
      "- All person_ids unique?:", ifelse(all_unique_conditions, "Yes", "No"), "\n\n")
  
  # Determine overlap between the two datasets:
  ids_cope = unique(cope_auo_unique$person_id)
  ids_conditions = unique(conditions_df$person_id)
  
  common_ids = intersect(ids_cope, ids_conditions)
  n_common = length(common_ids)
  
  only_in_cope = setdiff(ids_cope, ids_conditions)
  n_only_in_cope =length(only_in_cope)
  
  only_in_conditions = setdiff(ids_conditions, ids_cope)
  n_only_in_conditions = length(only_in_conditions)
  
  cat("Overlap between cope_auo_unique and conditions_df:\n",
      "- Common person_ids:", n_common, "\n",
      "- IDs only in cope_auo_unique:", n_only_in_cope, "\n",
      "- IDs only in conditions_df:", n_only_in_conditions, "\n")
  
  
  # Count unique participants across geographic locations
  participant_counts = cope_auo_ps %>%
    count(RegionName) %>%
    filter(!is.na(RegionName))  # Remove NA values from RegionName
  
  print(participant_counts, n = 50)
  
  # Determining completed and missing values for each outcome window (May, June, July)
  print(
    cope_auo_ps %>%
      summarise(
        total_rows = n(),
        complete_may = sum(!is.na(gad_score_avg_may)),
        missing_may = sum(is.na(gad_score_avg_may)),
        percent_complete_may = mean(!is.na(gad_score_avg_may)) * 100,
        percent_missing_may = mean(is.na(gad_score_avg_may)) * 100,
        complete_june = sum(!is.na(gad_score_avg_june)),
        missing_june = sum(is.na(gad_score_avg_june)),
        percent_complete_june = mean(!is.na(gad_score_avg_june)) * 100,
        percent_missing_june = mean(is.na(gad_score_avg_june)) * 100,
        complete_july = sum(!is.na(gad_score_avg_july)),
        missing_july = sum(is.na(gad_score_avg_july)),
        percent_complete_july = mean(!is.na(gad_score_avg_july)) * 100,
        percent_missing_july = mean(is.na(gad_score_avg_july)) * 100
      ),
    width = Inf
  )
  
  # Removing any rows with missing values in exposures 
  cope_auo_ps = cope_auo_ps %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(C1M_School_closing) &
        !is.na(C2M_Workplace_closing) &
        !is.na(C3M_Cancel_public_events) &
        !is.na(C4M_Restrictions_on_gatherings) &
        !is.na(C5M_Close_public_transport) &
        !is.na(C6M_Stay_at_home_requirements) &
        !is.na(C7M_Restrictions_on_internal_movement)
    )
  
  # Subset for May
  cope_auo_may = cope_auo_ps %>%
    filter(!is.na(gad_score_avg_may))
  
  
  # Subset for June
  cope_auo_june = cope_auo_ps %>%
    filter(!is.na(gad_score_avg_june))
  
  # Subset for July
  cope_auo_july = cope_auo_ps %>%
    filter(!is.na(gad_score_avg_july))
  
  # Create a function to analyze missing values and complete cases
  analyze_missing_values = function(data) {
    # Calculate complete cases
    complete_rows = data %>%
      select(insurance, income, employment, 
             education, sex, age_2020) %>%
      complete.cases() %>%
      sum()
    
    # Calculate percentage of complete cases
    total_rows = nrow(data)
    percent_complete = (complete_rows / total_rows) * 100
    
    # Original missing values analysis
    missing_summary = data %>%
      summarise(
        total_rows = n(),
        complete_rows = complete_rows,
        percent_complete_rows = percent_complete,
        
        # Health Insurance
        missing_health_insurance = sum(is.na(insurance)),
        percent_missing_health_insurance = mean(is.na(insurance)) * 100,
        
        # Household Income
        missing_household_income = sum(is.na(income)),
        percent_missing_household_income = mean(is.na(income)) * 100,
        
        # Employment
        missing_employment = sum(is.na(employment)),
        percent_missing_employment = mean(is.na(employment)) * 100,
        
        # Education
        missing_education = sum(is.na(education)),
        percent_missing_education = mean(is.na(education)) * 100,
        
        # Gender
        missing_gender = sum(is.na(sex)),
        percent_missing_gender = mean(is.na(sex)) * 100,
        
        # Age
        missing_age = sum(is.na(age_2020)),
        percent_missing_age = mean(is.na(age_2020)) * 100
      )
    
    return(missing_summary)
  }
  
  # Analyze missing values for each time period
  cat("\nMissing values analysis for full unique dataset:\n")
  analyze_missing_values(cope_auo_ps)
  
  cat("\nMissing values analysis for May subset:\n")
  analyze_missing_values(cope_auo_may)
  
  cat("\nMissing values analysis for June subset:\n")
  analyze_missing_values(cope_auo_june)
  
  cat("\nMissing values analysis for July subset:\n")
  analyze_missing_values(cope_auo_july)
  
  # Additional detailed analysis for July subset
  july_complete_cases = cope_auo_july %>%
    select(insurance, income, employment, 
           education, sex, age_2020) %>%
    complete.cases()

  # Function to add stringency. Hard coded relevant exposures inside, to change if selected windows change
  add_stringency_to_cope = function(cope_data, stringency_index = "march_15_june_30") {
    # Determine which stringency data and column to use based on the stringency_index parameter
    if (stringency_index == "march_15_june_30") {
      stringency_data = stringency_march_15_june_30
      stringency_column = "stringency_march_15_june_30"  # This is the column name in the data
    } else if (stringency_index == "march_22_may_23") {
      stringency_data = stringency_march_22_may_23
      stringency_column = "stringency_march_22_may_23"
    } else if (stringency_index == "april_12_may_23") {
      stringency_data = stringency_april_12_may_23
      stringency_column = "stringency_april_12_may_23"
    } else {
      stop("Invalid stringency_index. Must be one of 'march_15_june_30', 'march_22_may_23', or 'april_12_may_23'.")
    }
    
    # Create a copy of cope_data to avoid modifying the original
    cope_data_w_stringency = cope_data
    
    # Convert RegionName to character for matching
    region_names_char = as.character(cope_data_w_stringency$RegionName)
    
    # Create a lookup table from state name to stringency value
    state_to_stringency = setNames(
      stringency_data[[stringency_column]],
      stringency_data$state
    )
    
    # Check if all region names are in the stringency data
    missing_regions = setdiff(unique(region_names_char), names(state_to_stringency))
    if (length(missing_regions) > 0) {
      warning("Some regions in cope_data do not have matching stringency data: ", 
              paste(missing_regions, collapse = ", "))
    }
    
    # Add the stringency column to cope_data_w_stringency
    # Use the original stringency column name
    cope_data_w_stringency[[stringency_column]] <- 
      state_to_stringency[region_names_char]
    
    return(cope_data_w_stringency)
  }
  
  # Calling function to add stringency index to df 
  cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency = add_stringency_to_cope(cope_auo_july_no_miss, stringency_keys[i])
  
  # New age groups

  gad_quantiles = quantile(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency$gad_score_july, probs = 0:3/3, na.rm = TRUE)
  print(gad_quantiles) # 0, 1, 5, 21
  
  # Create GAD-7 tertile bins using quantile values (specified above)
  cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency$gad_category = cut(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency$gad_score_july,
                                    breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 21),
                                    labels = c("None", "Minimal", "Mild_Severe"),

  cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency$gad_category = cut(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency$gad_score_july,

    cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency$RegionName %in% c("Montana", "Wyoming", "Colorado", "Utah", "Idaho", "Nevada", "New Mexico") ~ "Mountain_West",
    cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency$RegionName %in% c("Oregon", "Washington", "Alaska", "Hawaii") ~ "Pacific_Northwest",
    TRUE ~ "Other_States"

  strata_counts = table(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency$strata_var)

    print("Remaining small strata:")
    print(small_strata)
  }
  
  ################################
  # MANUAL STRATIFIED SAMPLING IMPLEMENTATION
  ################################
  
  # The initial_split() function from rsample failed to execute stratified sampling despite multiple attempts to consolidate regional groupings and adjust the pool parameter. 
  # The function's default behavior requires a minimum threshold of observations within each stratum that appears to be overly conservative for our purposes.
  # This issue persisted, even with pool = 0.1, which should allow strata representing as little as 10% of the dataset.
  #
  # This manual implementation addresses these limitations by ensuring that each combination of geographic region (region_final) and GAD-7 category (gad_category) maintains 
  # proportional representation across training and testing datasets. 
  # The floor() function determines training set sizes within  ach stratum by rounding down to the nearest integer, which prevents fractional allocations 
  # This also ensures that smaller strata contribute at least some observations to both datasets when possible.
  #
  
  # Set seed for reproducibility
  set.seed(42)
  
  # Manual stratified sampling split
  stratified_data = cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency %>%
    
    # Group observations by geographic region and anxiety severity level
    group_by(region_final, gad_category) %>%
    
    # Randomly shuffle observations within each combination of region and GAD category
    # This prevents any bias from the ordering of rows in the original data 
    mutate(random_order = runif(n())) %>%
    arrange(random_order) %>%
    
    # Determine how many observations from each stratum go to training vs testing
    # Using floor ensures we get whole numbers and maintain the 50/50 split intention
    mutate(
      stratum_size = n(),
      train_size = floor(stratum_size * 0.50),
      train_flag = row_number() <= train_size
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Creating training and testing datasets
  train_data = stratified_data %>% filter(train_flag == TRUE)
  test_data = stratified_data %>% filter(train_flag == FALSE)
  
  # Display overall split sizes
  cat("Total observations:", nrow(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency), "\n")
  cat("Training set:", nrow(train_data), "\n") 
  cat("Testing set:", nrow(test_data), "\n")
  cat("Training proportion:", round(nrow(train_data) / nrow(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency), 3), "\n")
  cat("Testing proportion:", round(nrow(test_data) / nrow(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency), 3), "\n")
  

  # COMPARISON: MANUAL VS TIDYMODELS APPROACH ----------------
  
  # Adding tidymodels approach for comparison
  set.seed(42)
  data_split_tidymodels = initial_split(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency, prop = 0.50, strata = "strata_var", pool = 0.05)
  train_data_tidymodels = training(data_split_tidymodels)
  test_data_tidymodels = testing(data_split_tidymodels)
  
  # Comparing overall split sizes
  cat("Manual Method - Training:", nrow(train_data), "Testing:", nrow(test_data), "\n")
  cat("Tidymodels Method - Training:", nrow(train_data_tidymodels), "Testing:", nrow(test_data_tidymodels), "\n\n")
  
  
  # VERIFICATION CHECK -----------------------------
  
  # Verify stratification across regions - comparing both methods 
  # Counts and proportions are kept separate for better readability 
  verifying_state_stratification_counts = bind_rows(
    # Manual method results
    train_data %>% 
      count(region_final) %>% 
      mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "training"),
    test_data %>% 
      count(region_final) %>% 
      mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "testing"),
    # Tidymodels method results
    train_data_tidymodels %>% 
      count(region_final) %>% 
      mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "training"),
    test_data_tidymodels %>% 
      count(region_final) %>% 
      mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "testing")
  ) %>%
    select(region_final, method, dataset, n) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = c(method, dataset), values_from = n, names_sep = "_")
  
  verifying_state_stratification_proportions = bind_rows(
    # Manual method results
    train_data %>% 
      count(region_final) %>% 
      mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "training", proportion = n / sum(n)),
    test_data %>% 
      count(region_final) %>% 
      mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "testing", proportion = n / sum(n)),
    # Tidymodels method results
    train_data_tidymodels %>% 
      count(region_final) %>% 
      mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "training", proportion = n / sum(n)),
    test_data_tidymodels %>% 
      count(region_final) %>% 
      mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "testing", proportion = n / sum(n))
  ) %>%
    select(region_final, method, dataset, proportion) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = c(method, dataset), values_from = proportion, names_sep = "_")
  
  print("Regional Stratification - Sample Counts:")
  print(verifying_state_stratification_counts)
  print("Regional Stratification - Proportions:")
  print(verifying_state_stratification_proportions)
  
  # Verify stratification across GAD-7 categories - comparing both methods
  gad_verification_counts = bind_rows(
    # Manual method results
    train_data %>% 
      count(gad_category) %>% 
      mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "training"),
    test_data %>% 
      count(gad_category) %>% 
      mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "testing"),
    # Tidymodels method results
    train_data_tidymodels %>% 
      count(gad_category) %>% 
      mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "training"),
    test_data_tidymodels %>% 
      count(gad_category) %>% 
      mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "testing")
  ) %>%
    select(gad_category, method, dataset, n) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = c(method, dataset), values_from = n, names_sep = "_")
  
  gad_verification_proportions = bind_rows(
    # Manual method results
    train_data %>% 
      count(gad_category) %>% 
      mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "training", proportion = n / sum(n)),
    test_data %>% 
      count(gad_category) %>% 
      mutate(method = "manual", dataset = "testing", proportion = n / sum(n)),
    # Tidymodels method results
    train_data_tidymodels %>% 
      count(gad_category) %>% 
      mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "training", proportion = n / sum(n)),
    test_data_tidymodels %>% 
      count(gad_category) %>% 
      mutate(method = "tidymodels", dataset = "testing", proportion = n / sum(n))
  ) %>%
    select(gad_category, method, dataset, proportion) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = c(method, dataset), values_from = proportion, names_sep = "_")
  
  print("GAD-7 Category Stratification - Sample Counts:")
  print(gad_verification_counts)
  print("GAD-7 Category Stratification - Proportions:")
  print(gad_verification_proportions)
  
  # Verify stratification within each stratum - manual method only
  stratum_verification = stratified_data %>%
    group_by(region_final, gad_category) %>%
    summarise(
      total_n = n(),
      train_n = sum(train_flag),
      test_n = sum(!train_flag),
      train_prop = mean(train_flag),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(total_n)
  
  print("Stratum-Level Verification (Manual Method):")
  print(stratum_verification)
  
  # PERFORMING RERANDOMIZATION TO SELECT THE RANDOMIZATION WITH THE LOWEST AUC --------------------------------------------------
  
  
  cat("=== Rerandomization to determine 'optimal' train/test split ===\n")
  
  # Define list of covariates for balance assessment
  # These are the key predictors we want balanced between train/test sets
  balance_covariates = c(
    "age_2020", "home", "maritalstatus", "race", "education", "employment", 
    "insurance", "anxiety_disorder_before_covid_lifetime", "anxiety_disorder_1yr_before_covid", 
    "sex", "birthplace", "generalized_anxiety_disorder_before_covid_lifetime",
    "generalized_anxiety_disorder_1yr_before_covid", "gad_score_avg_july",
    "observation_wt_trim"
  )
  
  # Check which covariates exist in the data
  existing_covariates = intersect(balance_covariates, names(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency))
  missing_covariates = setdiff(balance_covariates, names(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency))
  
  if(length(missing_covariates) > 0) {
    cat("Missing covariates for balance analysis:", paste(missing_covariates, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }
  
  cat("Analyzing balance for", length(existing_covariates), "covariates:\n")
  cat(paste(existing_covariates, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")
  
  # Perform rerandomization analysis to select optimal split
  cat("Running rerandomization analysis...\n")
  rerand_results = perform_rerandomization(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency, n_randomizations = 20, method = "manual")
  
  # Store results and full dataframe
  assign(paste0("rerand_results", tolower(suffixes[i])), rerand_results)
  assign(paste0("cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency", tolower(suffixes[i])), copy(cope_auo_july_no_miss_w_stringency))
  
}
```

# Filter for best results across selected exposure windows


```{r}
# Initialize an empty list to hold intermediate dataframes
results_list <- list()

# Loop through suffixes
for (i in seq_along(suffixes)) {
  suffix <- tolower(suffixes[i])
  varname <- paste0("rerand_results", suffix)
  df <- get(varname)$all_results[, c("seed", "auc", "model_converged")]

  # Rename columns with suffix
  colnames(df) <- paste0(c("seed", "auc", "model_converged"), suffix)

  results_list[[suffix]] <- df
}

# Merge all dataframes by position (not by key) using cbind
combined_df <- Reduce(function(x, y) cbind(x, y), results_list)

# Compute row-wise average of all AUC columns
auc_cols <- grep("^auc_", colnames(combined_df))
combined_df$average_auc <- rowMeans(combined_df[, auc_cols], na.rm = TRUE)

```


```{r}
# Get best split

# Find best randomization: lowest AUC indicates best balance
best_randomization = combined_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(average_auc)) %>%
  slice_min(average_auc, n = 1) %>%
  slice(1)  # In case of ties, take the first

# View
print(best_randomization)

# Extract seed
seed_cols <- grep("^seed_", names(best_randomization), value = TRUE)
final_seed <- unique(unlist(best_randomization[, seed_cols]))
```



```{r}
# Match seed to get splits for all exposure windows

for (i in seq_along(period_keys)) {
  
  ## get results
  suffix <- tolower(suffixes[i])
  varname <- paste0("rerand_results", suffix)
  rerand_results <- get(varname)
  
  ## match index and split
  matching_index <- which(
    sapply(rerand_results$all_splits, function(x) x$seed == final_seed)
  )
  
  matching_split <- rerand_results$all_splits[[matching_index]]
  
  ## Extract training and testing sets
  train_data_df = matching_split$train
  test_data_df  = matching_split$test
  
  assign(paste0("train_data_df", tolower(suffixes[i])), copy(train_data_df))
  assign(paste0("test_data_df", tolower(suffixes[i])), copy(test_data_df))
  
}
```
